profilePeriod: Public record through 2026-10-03; concrete 2024 platform, explicitly dated earlier record, and 2025–2026 statements. No later comprehensive replacement platform located.
scopeNote: Question answers are independent source-constrained simulations, not statements Harris actually made. Distinguish direct evidence from cautious inference for hypothetical policies. Dedicated searches covered every axis; cross-checks include independent AP and Forward reporting and first-person CNN testimony.

sources.title: Harris-Walz economic policy book
sources.evidence: Private homebuilding, small-business incentives, ACA/Medicare protection, antitrust, emergency price-gouging ban, industrial investment, local housing innovation fund.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Economic Club speech transcript
sources.evidence: Capitalism and competitive markets alongside worker protection; action against unfair Chinese trade and strategic manufacturing investment.

sources.title: AP independent economic-policy reporting
sources.evidence: Corroborates pro-business middle-class platform and opposition to blanket tariffs; distinguishes regulation from communism.

sources.title: Douglas border speech
sources.evidence: Supports more border personnel, fentanyl scanners, stronger asylum restrictions and removal of unlawful entrants; also legal immigration, DREAMers, earned citizenship and rejection of scapegoating.

sources.title: Convening with voting-rights leaders
sources.evidence: National Freedom to Vote Act and John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act; work with diverse voting-rights constituencies.

sources.title: Democratic nomination acceptance speech
sources.evidence: Free elections, rule of law, peaceful transfer; federal reproductive protections; military superiority, NATO/Ukraine support, Israeli defence alongside ceasefire and Palestinian self-determination.

sources.title: Munich Security Conference position
sources.evidence: Rejects isolationism and unilateralism; supports NATO and continued US global leadership.

sources.title: Gun-violence and background-check press call
sources.evidence: Supports expanded background checks and federal gun-violence prevention.

sources.title: Criminal-justice reform pool report
sources.evidence: Promotes rehabilitation, reentry, accountability of law enforcement and civil-rights protections alongside public safety.

sources.title: Marijuana reform roundtable
sources.evidence: Calls for reform of marijuana scheduling and criticises racially unequal possession penalties.

sources.title: California DOJ marriage-equality statement
sources.evidence: Declined to defend Proposition 8 and sought immediate restoration of same-sex marriage across California.

sources.title: CNN presidential town hall transcript
sources.evidence: Daily prayer and Christian upbringing; faith guides service to others. Defends bodily autonomy and now rejects a fracking ban, while supporting clean energy.

sources.title: London AI speech
sources.evidence: Supports AI innovation with safeguards for privacy, discrimination, deepfakes and public safety; international coordination rather than unregulated acceleration.

sources.title: First-person 107 Days afterword excerpt
sources.evidence: Opposes authoritarianism, military deployment against civilians, sweeping tariffs and religious nationalism; supports social programmes, science, clean energy and peaceful popular mobilisation. Criticises institutional capitulation without endorsing dictatorship.

sources.title: Forward reporting on 107 Days
sources.evidence: Retrospective account of frustration with Netanyahu and Palestinian suffering; supports ceasefire and two-state settlement. Does not establish a new universal arms-embargo policy.

sources.title: Reported first-person Venezuela statement
sources.evidence: Condemned the Venezuela operation despite opposing Maduro; cited legality, troop risk and costs. Evidence against automatic support for regime-change wars.

sources.title: Original publisher: The Truths We Hold
sources.evidence: Political memoir with policy content, originally published in 2019.

sources.title: Brazilian publisher: As verdades que nos movem
sources.evidence: Confirms Brazilian title and translation release; catalogue year must remain original 2019.

sources.title: Official portrait by Lawrence Jackson
sources.evidence: US federal government official photograph, public domain; downloaded and compressed with repository script.

sources.title: California DOJ death-penalty appeal statement
sources.evidence: Appealed invalidation of California death penalty on legal grounds; institutional litigation is not proof of personal endorsement.

sources.title: AP on policy evolution, republished by PBS
sources.evidence: Documents personal death-penalty opposition and refusal to seek it as DA, followed by defence of existing law as AG. Historical record includes differences between stated reform goals and prosecution decisions.

sources.title: CNN 2019 town hall
sources.evidence: Favours not criminalising sex workers treated as exploited people, while prosecuting pimps and johns; not blanket legalisation of commercial sex.

sources.title: Axios on unconfirmed 2024 position
sources.evidence: Campaign declined to clarify whether 2019 support for sex-work decriminalisation remains current.

estrutura.evidence: National guarantees for voting and abortion alongside state/local housing implementation and incentives. Federalism with national rights floors; no evidence for abolishing states or secession.

representacao.evidence: Elections, peaceful transfer, expanded voting access and checks on executive power. Criticism of failed institutions in 2025 calls for mobilisation and democratic reform, not rule by decree.

poder.evidence: Institutional policing, border enforcement and gun regulation coexist with rehabilitation, cannabis reform, rights safeguards and opposition to political repression. Neither police abolition nor unlimited surveillance. Personal death-penalty opposition coexists with defence of existing law as attorney general; no inferred support for extending executions. Sex-work decriminalisation testimony targets exploitation, not blanket legalisation.

imigracao.evidence: Pluralist immigrant society, legal migration and citizenship routes coexist with tighter entry and asylum rules. Do not equate border enforcement with cultural assimilation.

diplomacia.evidence: Strong armed forces and allied defence, constrained by negotiation, humanitarian protection and objections to unilateral regime change. Not pacifist or an advocate of every military operation.

intervencao.evidence: Active multilateral US leadership and allied support rather than isolationism; opposition to the 2026 Venezuela operation limits inference of unlimited intervention.

economia.evidence: Private enterprise, competition and entrepreneurship with ACA/Medicare/Social Security and publicly funded housing incentives. No wholesale nationalisation or general privatisation of public services.

controle.evidence: Antitrust, crisis price-gouging ban and industrial subsidies alongside competition, supply expansion and cutting unnecessary red tape. Regulated capitalism rather than command allocation or laissez-faire.

comercio.evidence: Opposes universal tariffs, supports international ties, but protects strategic manufacturing and responds to unfair Chinese trade. Neither unrestricted free trade nor autarky.

religiao.evidence: Public Christian faith informs service; supports religious pluralism, personal choice and rejects religious nationalism. Personal faith must not become presumed state religion; family ancestry alone is not a political religious affiliation.

moral.evidence: Reproductive autonomy and same-sex marriage; reform of marijuana penalties. Cultural progressivism rather than religiously mandated morality.

tecnologia.evidence: AI, advanced manufacturing, scientific research and clean energy with safety regulation. Rejection of fracking ban qualifies environmental positions; no evidence for unrestricted transhumanism.

religionsDecision.reason: Computed religiao score is 54.8 (>35), so apply the repository default for a secular political programme. Acknowledged public Christian faith does not establish a strong confessional political programme; do not tag Hinduism or Judaism from family background.

bookDecision.reason: Author-written political memoir with substantive justice, healthcare, economic and security policy, not merely personal reminiscence; well-established Brazilian edition.

probableNeighbours.joe-biden: Shared governing record, but evaluate Harris independently, including reproductive-rights emphasis, prosecutors reform/security tension, market/entrepreneurship proposals and later opposition to unilateral war.
probableNeighbours.barack-obama: Same broad liberal family; do not copy. Harris has her own documented border/asylum proposals, industrial strategy and public faith.
probableNeighbours.bernie-sanders: Harris explicitly supports capitalism and private entrepreneurship rather than treating all major industries as public property.

audit.method: Single independent quality-model subagent; 240 individual answers and five archetypes; repository validator passed with proximity warnings.
audit.similarityReview: Validator passes (blocking threshold 97%) but NEW_PROFILE.md flags >=95% similarity as redundant. User reviewed the exact similarity warning, edited the PR description with a prominence rationale, and explicitly authorized creating a ready-for-review PR on 2026-10-03. Retain the profile with the documented overlap; no answers adjusted to increase distance.
audit.inferenceBoundary: Healthy brain implants/genetic enhancement, autonomous weapons, religious holiday/tax/symbol details, diet ethics and Brazil-specific quotas use cautious simulated preferences rather than documented proposals.
